epidemiological_finding: Short BFlh fascicle length is a modifiable HSI risk factor
sim_metric: d(peak fascicle strain)/d(fascicle factor); strain at x0.70 vs x1.20

documented_direction: risk rises as length drops below ~10.6 cm
sim_metric: model BFlh optimal fibre length; sweep range vs threshold
sim_evidence: L0=11.8 cm; sweep 8.3-14.2 cm brackets 10.6 cm (spans threshold)

epidemiological_finding: Short-fascicle athletes are not slower ('fast but fragile')
sim_metric: d(top speed)/d(fascicle factor); speed range over sweep

epidemiological_finding: Weak eccentric knee-flexor strength is a risk factor
sim_metric: strength sweep: d(peak strain), d(speed), d(ecc work) / d(strength)
verdict: REFINED: strength routes to performance & eccentric-work capacity, not peak stretch strain (two risk factors act via distinct paths)

epidemiological_finding: Biceps femoris long head is the most frequently injured hamstring
documented_direction: BFlh carries the greatest injurious load
sim_metric: active eccentric fibre work per hamstring at top speed (Nominal)
sim_evidence: bifemlh 16.5 J = highest of biarticular (semimem 11.8, semiten 6.0 J); rank bifemlh/semimem/semiten

epidemiological_finding: Sprint HSIs occur in terminal/late swing
documented_direction: peak lengthening in swing, not stance
sim_metric: phase of peak fascicle strain (all biarticular hams)
sim_evidence: peak strain in SWING for all biarticular hams: True

epidemiological_finding: Nordic/eccentric training reduces HSI (~51%) by lengthening fascicles
sim_metric: fascicle sweep, protective direction: peak strain & passive force at x1.10-1.20

epidemiological_finding: Prior injury and older age are the strongest (non-modifiable) predictors
sim_metric: not represented (no tissue-damage memory or ageing in the model)
